content: 1. The use of mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of elvitegravir by influencing the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug due to the potential for serious interactions. 2. Mitotane decreases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 3. Co-administration of elvitegravir with CYP3A inducers may lead to reduced plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and/or a concomitantly administered protease inhibitor, resulting in loss of therapeutic efficacy and potential resistance. Avoid such combinations or use alternative drugs. 4. Nafcillin reduces the levels or effects of elvitegravir by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug to maintain therapeutic effectiveness. 5. Elvitegravir decreases naloxone levels through an unknown mechanism. No dose adjustment of buprenorphine/naloxone is required, but patients should be closely monitored for sedation and cognitive effects. 6. Nefazodone increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely when co-administering these drugs. 7. Nelfinavir increases elvitegravir levels by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is advised due to the potential for increased drug levels. 8. Nevirapine decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 9. Nicardipine increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 10. Orlistat decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently, and discontinue orlistat if an increased HIV viral load is confirmed. 11. Oxcarbazepine reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 12. Pentobarbital decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to maintain therapeutic efficacy. 13. Phenobarbital reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative drug to prevent loss of therapeutic effect. 14. Phenytoin decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to maintain therapeutic efficacy. 15. Posaconazole increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 16. Primidone reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 17. Quinidine increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 18. Elvitegravir increases quizartinib levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce quizartinib dosage when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors, and resume the previous dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor. 19. Ribociclib increases elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of significant interactions. 20. Rifabutin decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to maintain therapeutic efficacy. 21. Rifampin reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 22. Rifapentine decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to maintain therapeutic efficacy. 23. Ritonavir increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 24. Rucaparib increases elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Dosage adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 25. St. John’s Wort decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug to prevent therapeutic failure. 26. Stiripentol affects elvitegravir levels by acting as both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor co-administered CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects, and adjust dosages as needed. 27. Tazemetostat decreases elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for therapeutic efficacy. 28. Tecovirimat reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by acting as a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 29. Tipranavir may increase elvitegravir levels, but data are insufficient to alter current dosing recommendations. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 150 mg orally once daily with tipranavir/ritonavir 500/200 mg orally twice daily. 30. Tucatinib increases elvitegravir levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose and monitor closely. 31. Ublituximab decreases elvitegravir effects through immunosuppressive actions, increasing the risk of infection. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Voclosporin and elvitegravir co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed to mitigate risks. 33. Voriconazole increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for potential toxicity. 34. Elvitegravir decreases warfarin levels or effects by influencing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely for anticoagulant efficacy. 35. Zinc reduces elvitegravir levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer elvitegravir 2 hours before or 6 hours after polyvalent cation-containing products to avoid interaction. 36. Elvitegravir is an integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) that prevents the integration of HIV-1 DNA into host genomic DNA, thereby blocking the formation of the HIV-1 provirus and halting viral replication. 37.
